evidence.quote:
TypeLLM brings type-safe generation to existing autoregressive LLMs without changing their architecture or weights. Inspired by [TypeSafe AI's Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev), it lets models retain their native thinking and free-form generation while producing schema-guaranteed outputs through JSON Schema. Built on [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), TypeLLM also supports richer interaction patterns beyond independent typed decisions.


### Supported output types

**String · Integer · Number · Boolean · Enum choice** — See [schemas and examples](#output-types).

claims.text: Inspired by Jev, it retains free text and optional reasoning and supports dependencies between output fields.

evidence.quote: TypeLLM brings type-safe generation to existing autoregressive LLMs without changing their architecture or weights. Inspired by [TypeSafe AI's Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev), it lets models retain their native thinking and free-form generation while producing schema-guaranteed outputs through JSON Schema. Built on [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), TypeLLM also supports richer interaction patterns beyond independent typed decisions.

1. **No out-of-schema hallucinations** — Choices stay within the allowed values.
2. **Negligible output-token cost** — Single-token categorical selection and bounded numeric decoding; optional thinking adds tokens.
3. **Shared-prefix reuse** — KV caching avoids reprocessing shared context.
4. **Dependency-aware execution** — Independent fields run together; declare `depends_on` to form a dependency graph.
5. **Made for open autoregressive LLMs** — Use compatible models you already serve with SGLang.
6. **Supports thinking mode** — Enable reasoning before the final constrained answer.
7. **Image input** — Pass images to vision-language models alongside the text context. See [Image input](#image-input).
8. **Permutation averaging** — Reduce option-order bias on explicit enum questions with balanced, sampled or exhaustive orderings. See the [docs](https://typellm.ai/docs/probabilities#permutation-averaging).

claims.text: Serve a compatible model with SGLang, then submit context and typed questions through TypeLLMClient.

evidence.quote:
### 1. Serve a model with SGLang

Use [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) to configure and serve a
compatible autoregressive model on your local GPU server. This example uses
Qwen3.8-27B; follow the
[Qwen3.8-27B SGLang deployment guide](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B)
to start it with prefix caching enabled.

See [Supported models](#supported-models) for tested checkpoints and thinking behavior.

### 2. Run TypeLLM

```bash
pip install -U typellm
```

Point `TypeLLMClient` at the SGLang server's HTTP endpoint:

```python
from typellm import TypeLLMClient

client = TypeLLMClient(
    "http://127.0.0.1:30000",
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
)

claims.text: Schema constraints govern allowed values; text, numeric outputs and optional reasoning still generate multiple tokens.

evidence.quote:
1. **No out-of-schema hallucinations** — Choices stay within the allowed values.
2. **Negligible output-token cost** — Single-token categorical selection and bounded numeric decoding; optional thinking adds tokens.
3. **Shared-prefix reuse** — KV caching avoids reprocessing shared context.
4. **Dependency-aware execution** — Independent fields run together; declare `depends_on` to form a dependency graph.
5. **Made for open autoregressive LLMs** — Use compatible models you already serve with SGLang.
6. **Supports thinking mode** — Enable reasoning before the final constrained answer.

Enum and boolean fields use one output token each. Numeric, text, and optional
thinking outputs use multiple tokens.

tr.summary: TypeLLM mevcut otoregresif modellere ağırlık veya mimari değişikliği yapmadan JSON Schema kısıtlı çıktılar ekler. Jev’den esinlenir; serbest metni, isteğe bağlı akıl yürütmeyi ve çıktı alanları arasındaki bağımlılıkları destekler. SGLang ile uyumlu model sunun, ardından TypeLLMClient üzerinden bağlam ve türlenmiş soruları gönderin.

sections.heading: Ne işe yarar
sections.text: TypeLLM mevcut otoregresif modellere ağırlık veya mimari değişikliği yapmadan JSON Schema kısıtlı çıktılar ekler.

sections.heading: Jev’in rolü
sections.text: Jev’den esinlenir; serbest metni, isteğe bağlı akıl yürütmeyi ve çıktı alanları arasındaki bağımlılıkları destekler.

sections.heading: Kullanım
sections.text: SGLang ile uyumlu model sunun, ardından TypeLLMClient üzerinden bağlam ve türlenmiş soruları gönderin.

sections.heading: Sınırlamalar
sections.text: Şema izin verilen değerleri sınırlar; metin, sayısal çıktılar ve isteğe bağlı akıl yürütme birden fazla token üretir.

it.title: TypeLLM: generazione strutturata ispirata a Jev
it.h1: TypeLLM: generazione strutturata ispirata a Jev
it.description: TypeLLM aggiunge output vincolati ai modelli con SGLang. Ispirato a Jev, supporta anche testo libero, ragionamento e campi dipendenti.
it.summary: TypeLLM aggiunge output vincolati da JSON Schema a modelli autoregressivi esistenti senza modificarne pesi o architettura. Ispirato a Jev, conserva testo libero e ragionamento facoltativo e supporta dipendenze fra campi. Servi un modello compatibile con SGLang, poi invia contesto e domande tipizzate tramite TypeLLMClient.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: TypeLLM aggiunge output vincolati da JSON Schema a modelli autoregressivi esistenti senza modificarne pesi o architettura.

sections.heading: Il ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Ispirato a Jev, conserva testo libero e ragionamento facoltativo e supporta dipendenze fra campi.

sections.heading: Come usarlo
sections.text: Servi un modello compatibile con SGLang, poi invia contesto e domande tipizzate tramite TypeLLMClient.

sections.heading: Limiti
sections.text: Lo schema limita i valori consentiti; testo, numeri e ragionamento facoltativo generano comunque più token.
